input.reasoning_summary: The claim that P&G's first quarter of fiscal 2027 showed 'broad-based momentum' is contradicted by the evidence. While Q1 FY2027 (three months ended September 30, 2026) did show some positive indicators—net sales grew 4%, operating income grew 1%, and all five business segments posted positive sales growth—the overall picture contradicts the characterization of 'broad-based momentum.' Key profitability metrics deteriorated: gross margin decreased 160 basis points to 49.8%, operating margin decreased 70 basis points to 25.5%, and net earnings declined 1%. The term 'broad-based momentum' implies positive performance across multiple dimensions of the business, but the evidence shows a mixed picture with significant margin compression and declining earnings despite revenue growth. This pattern of declining profitability metrics contradicts the assertion of broad-based momentum.
